title: Sodium butyrate upregulates URAT1-mediated urate reabsorption in HK2 cells by activating FFAR2/p38 MAPK/ELK1/ARRB2 axis and relieving NF-kappaB-HNF1beta competitive binding.
authors: Cao, Cheng; Sun, Mubin; Li, Jiabao; Yuan, Zhenyu; Gu, Yuwei; Shao, Yufan; Wang, Lisheng; Jin, Xiaohua; Cheng, Yijie; Fan, Bo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丁酸钠通过FFAR2/p38 MAPK/ELK1/ARRB2轴调控URAT1表达，涉及NF-kappaB与HNF1beta在SLC22A12启动子上的竞争性结合，但核心是代谢调控与转录调控，非TF-DNA互作建模，且方法以湿实验为主，仅分子对接辅助，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Urate transporter 1 (URAT1, encoded by SLC22A12) is a key mediator of renal urate reabsorption and an important pharmacological target for urate-related disorders. Sodium butyrate (BuNa), a gut microbiota derived short-chain fatty acid, has been implicated in host metabolic regulation, but its role in renal urate transport remains unclear. Here, using molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assays, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry and multi-omics analyses, we identified free fatty acid receptor 2 (FFAR2) as a direct target of BuNa in renal proximal tubular HK2 cells . BuNa binding upregulated FFAR2 and promoted URAT1 expression and urate uptake via an FFAR2-dependent pathway. Mechanistically, BuNa/FFAR2 signaling acts via GNAQ to activate PLCbeta, generating diacylglycerol and engaging a PKC-dependent p38 MAPK/ELK1 cascade that upregulates arrestin beta 2 (ARRB2). ARRB2 directly binds to IkappaB, preventing its phosphorylation-dependent degradation, thereby stabilizing IkappaB and inhibiting NF-kappaB nuclear translocation. Within the SLC22A12 promoter, NF-kappaB (RELA/p50) and hepatocyte nuclear factor 1 beta (HNF1beta) compete for overlapping binding sites. By blocking NF-kappaB nuclear entry, BuNa relieves this competition, permitting HNF1beta-driven SLC22A12 transcription. Thus, BuNa enhances URAT1-mediated urate reabsorption in HK2 cells via an FFAR2/GNAQ/p38 MAPK/ELK1/ARRB2 axis that stabilizes IkappaB, suppresses NF-kappaB, and relieves the competitive binding between NF-kappaB and HNF1beta on the SLC22A12 promoter. These findings establish a previously unrecognized gut microbiota-kidney axis linking microbial BuNa to renal urate homeostasis through a novel transcriptional regulatory circuit.
abstract_zh: 尿酸盐转运蛋白1（URAT1，由SLC22A12编码）是肾脏尿酸盐重吸收的关键介导因子，也是尿酸盐相关疾病的重要药理靶点。丁酸钠（BuNa）作为一种肠道微生物来源的短链脂肪酸，已被认为参与宿主代谢调节，但其在肾脏尿酸盐转运中的作用仍不清楚。在此，通过分子对接、细胞热位移分析、免疫沉淀-质谱联用及多组学分析，我们鉴定出游离脂肪酸受体2（FFAR2）为BuNa在肾近端小管HK2细胞中的直接靶点。BuNa结合上调FFAR2，并通过FFAR2依赖性途径促进URAT1表达和尿酸盐摄取。机制上，BuNa/FFAR2信号通过GNAQ激活PLCbeta，生成二酰甘油并启动PKC依赖性p38 MAPK/ELK1级联反应，从而上调arrestin beta 2（ARRB2）。ARRB2直接结合IkappaB，阻止其磷酸化依赖性降解，从而稳定IkappaB并抑制NF-kappaB核转位。在SLC22A12启动子内，NF-kappaB（RELA/p50）和肝细胞核因子1 beta（HNF1beta）竞争重叠结合位点。通过阻断NF-kappaB核进入，BuNa解除这种竞争，允许HNF1beta驱动的SLC22A12转录。因此，BuNa通过FFAR2/GNAQ/p38 MAPK/ELK1/ARRB2轴增强HK2细胞中URAT1介导的尿酸盐重吸收，该轴稳定IkappaB、抑制NF-kappaB，并解除NF-kappaB与HNF1beta在SLC22A12启动子上的竞争性结合。这些发现确立了一个此前未被识别的肠道微生物-肾脏轴，通过一种新的转录调控回路将微生物BuNa与肾脏尿酸盐稳态联系起来。
